questions.q: What is the process of breaking down large, insoluble food molecules into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed into the blood?

Which organ produces bile, which is stored in the gall bladder to emulsify fats?

a: Absorption of digested food molecules into the blood and lymph

questions.q: Which enzyme present in saliva starts the breakdown of starch into maltose?
What is the main function of the large intestine (colon)?
a: Absorbing large amounts of mineral salts
Absorbing remaining water from undigested food residue

questions.q: What term describes the passage of digested food molecules through the wall of the intestine into the blood or lymph?

a: To kill harmful bacteria ingested with food and provide an optimum acidic pH for pepsin enzymes

To absorb water into the blood

questions.q: Which organ secretes digestive enzymes (amylase, trypsin, lipase) into the small intestine?
What is the function of bile produced by the liver?
a: To break down proteins into amino acids
To neutralize stomach acid and emulsify large fat droplets into smaller ones to increase surface area
To kill bacteria in the mouth

questions.q: What is egestion?
a: The removal of metabolic waste products like urea
The intake of food into the mouth
The passing out of undigested food waste (faeces) through the anus

questions.q: How are the inner walls of the small intestine specially adapted for efficient absorption of digested food?
a: They are covered in millions of tiny finger-like projections called villi and microvilli, providing a massive surface area
They lack blood vessels to keep food safe

questions.q: What is the function of the gall bladder?
a: To store and release bile into the small intestine

questions.q: Which digestive enzyme breaks down fats (lipids) into fatty acids and glycerol?
What happens to food in the mouth during mechanical (physical) digestion?
a: It is absorbed directly into the brain
It is chewed by teeth to increase surface area for enzymes

Which section of the alimentary canal connects the mouth to the stomach?
What are the tiny finger-like projections on the inner wall of the small intestine called?
Which of these is the correct order of food movement through the human digestive system?
a: Oesophagus -> Stomach -> Small intestine -> Large intestine -> Anus

questions.q: What is the function of capillaries inside each villus in the small intestine?
a: To absorb and transport digested glucose and amino acids into the bloodstream
To pump blood to the lungs

questions.q: What is the role of lacteals found inside villi?

questions.q: Why is it important that small intestine walls are only one cell thick?
a: To allow food to escape into the stomach
To provide a short diffusion distance for rapid absorption of nutrients

questions.q: What is ingestion?
a: The breakdown of food in the stomach
The chemical conversion of nutrients in cells
The taking of substances into the body through the mouth

questions.q: What prevents food from entering the trachea (windpipe) when swallowing?
a: The epiglottis folds down over the larynx

What is the optimum pH environment for stomach enzymes like pepsin to function efficiently?
Why does pancreatic juice contain sodium hydrogen carbonate?
a: To neutralize acidic chyme coming from the stomach, creating a neutral/alkaline pH for intestinal enzymes
